description: Canonical field contract for a ROLE QUALIFICATION: one capability contract naming an executable predicate, and one record of what a named binding was observed to do against it. bin/fm-qualification-lib.sh and bin/fm-qualification.sh are the only interpreters; their headers and --help own the mechanics. A record answers one question and only that question: on this exact binding, against this exact contract version, what was OBSERVED, and what would have to change materially before that observation stops applying.
why: Missing qualification was being treated as a captain decision. It is an engineering state: a candidate that may satisfy a blocked route is qualified empirically through a bounded representative workflow and that evidence is reused, rather than a task-specific floor exception being requested every time. The 2026-08-13 captain ruling states it directly - model names are bindings to capability contracts, not capability contracts themselves.
why_not_the_model_registry: config/models.json answers whether a model may be PAID FOR, REACHED, and RUN CONCURRENTLY, and it is local and gitignored because those are properties of one account on one machine. This register answers whether a binding was observed to DO a named job, which is a property of the binding against a contract and is worth shipping to every home. Folding the two would make an availability or billing fact able to grant a capability, and would make a capability record able to authorize spend. They are separate axes and axes below refuses collapsing them.

not_a_security_boundary.statement: A qualification record is a CAPABILITY record, not containment. It constrains which binding firstmate ROUTES a job to; it does not stop a binding that receives the job anyway from doing anything.
not_a_security_boundary.why: Every crewmate is launched with permission enforcement disabled (capabilities/catalog.json states the same fact and why). Nothing here refuses at execution time.
not_a_security_boundary.consequence: No decision may read a QUALIFIED record as a guarantee about a run. It records what was observed once, against named bytes, under named limitations.

result_vocabulary._rule: These five values are the whole vocabulary and no synonym is accepted. An unregistered word - inconclusive, unknown, pass, fail, true, false - makes a record INADMISSIBLE rather than being normalized, because the measured failure this register was built from was exactly a candidate emitting synonyms and an evaluator being tempted to read them charitably.
result_vocabulary.QUALIFIED: The contract's executable predicate ran against this binding, returned its own pass, and the required assignment-distinct adjudication returned a pass. This is the only value that admits a candidate.
result_vocabulary.FAILED: The predicate ran and rejected this binding. Observed-bad, and preserved as exclusion evidence; a later record never deletes it.
result_vocabulary.QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED: No applicable observation exists yet for this exact tuple, or one exists but does not carry the required adjudication. Missing evidence, NOT incapability, and never FAILED.
result_vocabulary.QUALIFICATION_STALE: An observation existed and a declared material freshness dependency changed, so it no longer applies. Stale evidence, NOT incapability, and never FAILED.
result_vocabulary.COULD_NOT_OBSERVE: The predicate, the adjudication, or a declared freshness dependency could not be observed at all. Nonterminal evidence uncertainty. It is never a pass, it never records a negative against the binding, and it never becomes a reputation.

derived_state_is_never_stored.rule: A record stores what was OBSERVED (`result`) and the dependencies that observation rests on. It never stores the state a reader should act on. The interpreter computes that state on every read from the record plus a fresh dependency observation.
derived_state_is_never_stored.why: A stored state is a state that keeps reading correct after the thing under it moved. That is the whole failure mode this register exists inside: an assertion that outlived its evidence.
computation: no applicable record for the tuple -> QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, citing any near-miss record for the same contract and model under a different harness or native effort
result COULD_NOT_OBSERVE -> COULD_NOT_OBSERVE, whatever the dependencies say
result FAILED with every declared dependency unchanged -> FAILED; the exclusion stands

result FAILED with a declared dependency materially changed -> QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED, with the prior FAILED record cited rather than removed. This line says the OBSERVATION no longer applies and says NOTHING about whether the binding may be invoked again; `separated_facts` below owns that, and reading this line as a permission is the defect that block was added to close
result QUALIFIED with a declared dependency materially changed -> QUALIFICATION_STALE
result QUALIFIED with a declared dependency unobservable -> COULD_NOT_OBSERVE
result QUALIFIED with every declared dependency observed unchanged -> QUALIFIED

separated_facts._description: The state above answers what was OBSERVED. Two more facts are computed from the same record and returned beside it, because reading the state as though it also answered them is a measured defect rather than a hypothetical one.
separated_facts.the_measured_defect: Two bindings held FAILED records against contract 1.1.0. A 1.2.0 generation was proposed. Because `contract_version` is a declared freshness dependency, EVERY FAILED record then computed QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED - which is the only classification `activate` accepts. Installing a contract generation would therefore have turned two bindings that were tried and rejected into automatically activatable ones. No contract file could fix that: the collapse is in the computation, and the repair is to separate the axes rather than to add a sixth state.

applicability.question: Does the observation still apply to the generation in force?

values.CURRENT: every declared freshness dependency is observed unchanged
values.STALE: a declared freshness dependency materially changed
values.COULD_NOT_OBSERVE: a declared freshness dependency could not be read at all

applicability.computed_from: the declared freshness dependencies alone, by exactly the fold the state uses. It is null when there is no record, because there is no observation whose currency to report.
applicability.three_values_not_two: A dependency nobody could read leaves applicability unobserved, and narrowing that into either CURRENT or STALE would report a gap as one of the two answers it is not. Same rule as everywhere else in this fleet.

retry_disposition.question: Is another invocation of this binding permitted?

values.permitted: nothing withholds one. Either no adverse observation stands against this tuple at all, or one does and the material predicate it failed has demonstrably changed.
values.not-permitted: an adverse observation stands against this tuple under a material predicate that has not changed. The invocation would only re-observe a settled failure, so it is refused rather than spent.
values.unknown: an adverse observation stands and whether its material predicate changed COULD NOT BE OBSERVED. It withholds the invocation exactly as `not-permitted` does, but the repair is to the REGISTER rather than to the binding, and no new finding is recorded against it.

retry_disposition.only_an_adverse_observation_withholds: Computed only for a record whose result is FAILED. A stale pass, a missing record and a could-not-observe all leave the disposition `permitted`, because refusing there would freeze a stale qualification forever and would make a first qualification of any tuple impossible.
computation: record carries no predicate_generation -> unknown. Which material predicate this binding failed was never recorded, so whether it has since changed cannot be observed. This is every record written before the field existed.
contract declares no executable_predicate.predicate_generation -> unknown, from the other side

the two generations are equal -> not-permitted. The predicate this binding was graded by is the one still in force, whatever the contract VERSION now reads. This is the rung that closes the defect above.
the generations differ and the predicate kind carries no generation manifest -> permitted
the generations differ and the generation in force declares no predicates_unchanged_from entry for the record's base manifest -> permitted

the generations differ, an entry exists, and every claim id in the record's failed_predicates appears in it -> not-permitted; the adverse observation is carried forward for claims the new generation declares unchanged
the generations differ, an entry exists, and at least one failed claim id is absent from it -> permitted; one changed claim it failed is enough, because the binding may now pass
the generations differ, an entry exists, and the record names no failed_predicates -> unknown; whether the claims it failed are among the carried-forward ones cannot be evaluated
a declared `disposition` on the record is then folded in, and may only make the answer STRICTER: not-permitted beats unknown beats permitted
retry_disposition.the_declaration_is_the_material_change_p: Absence of a `predicates_unchanged_from` entry means the predicate materially changed, so a retry is permitted. That is the honest default the governing law allows only through an EXPLICIT material-change predicate, and the declaration is that predicate read in the negative: a new generation that says nothing about a base generation's claims has replaced them. Silence about which generation a record was graded by is a different thing entirely and is never a permission - it is `unknown`.
retry_disposition.a_declared_disposition_never_grants: A record may declare a durable do-not-retry so refusing a known failed binding stops depending on firstmate remembering to. It may only withhold. A hand-written `permitted` never overrides a computed refusal, for exactly the reason `refused_keys` exists: a claim anyone can write is one that will eventually be written wrongly, and this is the claim that spends a model call on a binding already known to fail.

separated_facts.migration: A record carrying neither `predicate_generation` nor `disposition` keeps its current five-value state semantics unchanged, and its retry disposition reads `unknown`. Nothing already recorded is rewritten, reinterpreted or invalidated: the historical adverse observation stands exactly as it was, and what changes is only that it is no longer read as a permission to re-run the binding.
separated_facts.who_refuses_on_it: bin/fm-route-lib.sh keeps a candidate whose disposition is not `permitted` out of `promising` and reports it under its own blocker; bin/fm-qualification.sh activate refuses to spend a workflow on one; bin/fm-spawn.sh refuses the dispatch by name. Every one of them READS the disposition the interpreter computed and none re-derives it.

unrelated_bytes_are_not_a_dependency.rule: Freshness is computed ONLY from the dependencies a record declares. Nothing else invalidates it - not the repository head, not an unrelated tracked file, not a vendor or model label, not the passage of time unless the record declares a time bound.
unrelated_bytes_are_not_a_dependency.why: A register that goes stale on every commit is a register nobody can rely on, and the reflex repair is to stop checking it. The ruling names this explicitly: unrelated repository bytes do not invalidate qualification.

axes._rule: Nine independent axes. No axis may be read as another, and a contract declares exactly one. A capability that would grant a second axis is INADMISSIBLE rather than accepted with a note, because the collapse is the failure: an available model reading as a qualified one, or a qualified maker reading as an independent reviewer.

maker_qualification.question: Was this binding observed to DO the job?
maker_qualification.owner: qualifications/contracts/*.json with axis maker_qualification, interpreted by bin/fm-qualification-lib.sh

design_challenge.question: Was this binding observed to challenge a DESIGN before it is built?
design_challenge.separate_because: Challenging a plan and checking a diff are different jobs measured by different predicates. A route that requires both requires two records.

exact_change_review.question: Was this binding observed to review the EXACT CHANGE after it is made?
exact_change_review.separate_because: Same reason as above, from the other side. One reviewer may perform both only when it holds a QUALIFIED record for each and assignment independence still holds.

assignment_independence.question: Is the checker independent of the maker on THIS assignment?
assignment_independence.owner: bin/fm-qualification-lib.sh fm_qualification_independence, composing bin/fm-model-registry-lib.sh for the declared credential pool; bin/fm-independence-lib.sh owns the separate pipeline-derived per-run verdict
assignment_independence.separate_because: A binding can be perfectly qualified as a reviewer and still be the maker of the thing under review. Self-review is refused on this axis, never on the qualification axis.

provider_account_pool_identity.question: Which provider, account and credential pool does this binding actually draw on?
provider_account_pool_identity.separate_because: A harness name cannot answer it, and two bindings that differ by model can still share one billing window.

availability.question: Can the fleet reach this binding right now?
availability.owner: bin/fm-route-lib.sh over state/model-health.json, and bin/fm-capacity-lib.sh over quota-axi
availability.separate_because: An unavailable binding is a WAIT. Reading unavailability as unqualified would make every outage permanently degrade the routing table; reading availability as qualification is the mistake the ruling names - one vendor being reachable is not evidence that runtime engineering can proceed, and it is not evidence that it cannot when another binding satisfies the same predicates.

cost.question: Can this call cost money?
cost.separate_because: Cheapest and most capable are unrelated orderings, and a qualification record may never authorize spend.

entitlement.question: Will this account actually get an answer?
entitlement.separate_because: A model can be entitled and billable, or unentitled and free-if-it-worked. A qualification run proves neither.

attempt_custody_accounting.question: How many attempts has this work identity spent, and what are its custody bases?
attempt_custody_accounting.separate_because: A qualification workflow is its OWN work identity with its own bounded budget. It must never spend, reset or inherit the accounting of the work it unblocks.

contract._description: One capability contract: the reusable role and risk version a record binds to, and the executable predicate that decides it.

required.id: stable slug, unique across contracts; must match the file basename
required.role: UPPER_SNAKE role name, the reusable role half of the contract
required.risk_class: slug, the reusable risk half; role plus risk_class is the narrowest reusable scope a record may claim
required.contract_version: semantic version of THIS contract's own bytes. A record cites it, so a contract change is a freshness dependency rather than a silent redefinition.
required.axis: exactly one key from axes above
required.purpose: one sentence: what a QUALIFIED record on this contract means
required.grants: one sentence: what routing decision a QUALIFIED record is allowed to unblock
required.does_not_grant: non-empty array of one-sentence statements naming what it explicitly does not establish

optional.adjudication: adjudication object; see adjudication. Absent means no assignment-distinct adjudication is required, which is only lawful for a contract whose predicate is fully deterministic with no candidate-authored claim.
optional.required_freshness_dependencies: array of freshness_dependency_kinds keys a record on this contract MUST declare. A record missing one is INADMISSIBLE.
optional.note: free prose for a reader; never consumed

contract.predicate_generation_is_declared_on_the_: `executable_predicate.predicate_generation` is the sha256 digest of the MATERIAL predicate in force: the oracle program plus the candidate-visible claims package, and NOT the contract version and NOT the whole manifest. It is deliberately narrower than either, because a contract version moves for editorial reasons and a manifest digest moves when any packaged byte does, while the question it answers is whether the thing a candidate was graded against actually changed. It is optional: a contract declaring none leaves every adverse record's retry disposition `unknown`, which withholds a re-run rather than authorizing one.

vendor_neutrality.rule: A contract names a JOB, never who does it. The keys models, bindings, binding, providers, provider, vendors, vendor, harnesses, harness, and model are REFUSED outright, and no string value anywhere in a contract may equal a model or provider this home's routing config configures.
vendor_neutrality.why: The ruling's load-bearing sentence is that model names are bindings to capability contracts and not the contracts themselves. A contract that names a vendor is doctrine dressed as a predicate: it stops being re-runnable against the next candidate, which is the entire point of qualifying one.
vendor_neutrality.enforced_by: bin/fm-qualification.sh validate, and tests/fm-qualification.test.sh drives it red first

record._description: One observation of one binding against one contract. Records live in qualifications/records/ when they are worth shipping to every home, and in the gitignored data/qualifications/records/ overlay when the binding or evidence is captain-private. The overlay's absence is silent; a tracked record that cannot be read is COULD_NOT_OBSERVE.

required.id: stable slug, unique across the tracked register and the home overlay; must match the file basename
required.contract: id of the contract this observation was made against
required.contract_version: the contract_version observed. A record whose cited version differs from the contract's current one is STALE, not wrong.
required.binding: binding object: provider, model (fully qualified provider/model-id), harness, harness_version, native_effort. The record KEY is exactly contract, model, harness and native_effort; provider is implied by the required fully qualified model. harness_version records context but is not a key axis because harness semantics cannot be probed at record-read time; drift is bounded only by a declared harness_semantics dependency and its required time_bound. A different harness or native effort is a different tuple, while a different harness version is a later observation of the same tuple and must use supersedes.
required.result_evidence: one sentence naming what was observed to produce that result, and by which oracle
required.measured_context: the context actually measured during the run, as a positive integer of tokens, or exactly COULD_NOT_OBSERVE. An estimate is never substituted for a measurement.
required.observed_at: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) the observation was made
required.freshness_dependencies: non-empty array of dependency objects; see freshness_dependency_kinds
required.known_limitations: non-empty array of one-sentence statements. A record with nothing to declare here has not been examined; every real qualification run has a boundary.

optional.adjudication: adjudication_result object recording who graded this run and what they returned. Required in effect for any contract that declares adjudication.required true: without it the derived state is QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED however good the predicate result was.
optional.fixture: fixture object: identity, version, manifest_digest. Required in effect by a fixture_oracle predicate.
optional.evidence: array of paths or URLs POINTING AT retained raw evidence. Never the evidence itself.
optional.supersedes: id of a record this one replaces for the same tuple. The superseded record is retained, because deleting an adverse observation is how a register launders a failure.
optional.predicate_generation: sha256 digest of the MATERIAL predicate this observation was graded by, matching the contract's executable_predicate.predicate_generation at the time. It is what lets a later generation tell an observation it superseded from one it did not. Absent means unrecorded, which the interpreter reads as could-not-observe and never as a permission to re-run the binding.
optional.failed_predicates: non-empty array of the claim ids the predicate rejected, for a record whose result is FAILED. A later generation can only carry an adverse observation forward for claims it can NAME, so a record that names none cannot be evaluated against a carry-forward declaration.
optional.disposition: durable retry disposition object: `retry` (exactly `permitted` or `not-permitted-unchanged-predicate`), `reason` (one sentence), and `authority` (who settled it). This is the explicit do-not-retry representation, so refusing to re-run a known failed binding stops depending on firstmate remembering to. It may only ever make the computed disposition STRICTER; a declared `permitted` grants nothing.
optional.note: free prose for a reader; never consumed

record.refused_keys_why: A hand-written state must not be able to answer the question the interpreter computes. The interpreter refuses a record carrying any of these outright rather than ignoring them, because an ignored field still reads to a human as the answer. `score` and `rank` are refused for a second reason: scoring a handful of bindings on several axes from a bounded suite manufactures precision the evidence cannot support, and pass-or-fail against a contract is the honest granularity. `applicability` and `retry_disposition` are refused for the FIRST reason and are the two separated facts above: `disposition` is admitted alongside them because it is a declared INPUT that may only withhold, while `retry_disposition` is the computed ANSWER and a record asserting it would be asserting whether it is worth re-running itself.

adjudication._description: Declared on a contract, and recorded on a record.

contract_fields.required: boolean. True whenever the predicate consumes any claim the candidate itself authored.
contract_fields.adjudicator_contract: id of the contract an adjudicator must itself hold a QUALIFIED record for. An adjudicator that is not itself qualified for the grading job cannot grade.
contract_fields.independence_dimensions: array of independence dimensions that must hold between the maker binding and the adjudicator binding. binding is always required and is the self-review refusal; provider and pool are declared when the contract needs them.

record_fields.adjudicator_binding: the adjudicator's fully qualified model, or null when no adjudication was performed
record_fields.adjudicator_result: one key from result_vocabulary - what the adjudicator returned about the maker run
record_fields.evidence: one sentence or path pointing at the adjudication record

adjudication.self_review_is_refused: A record whose adjudicator_binding equals its own binding.model is INADMISSIBLE. No binding independently reviews its own mutation merely because it qualified as maker; the ruling says so outright, and a note in a report is not a mechanism.
adjudication.a_contract_may_require_two_roles: A route that requires both design_challenge and exact_change_review requires two QUALIFIED records. One reviewer may hold both, and may then perform both on one assignment, but only when assignment independence from the maker still holds for that assignment. Holding both records is never itself independence.

predicate_kinds._rule: A closed set. A contract naming any other kind is INADMISSIBLE. `executable` is the load-bearing word: a contract whose predicate is prose is a preference, and a preference cannot qualify anything.

fixture_oracle.description: A deterministic oracle outside the candidate's reach grades a candidate that ran in disposable state. The strongest kind available and the default.

args.manifest_digest: sha256 of the package manifest, so a record binds the exact bytes it was graded by
args.root: where the package resolves: `home:<relative path>` under FM_HOME, or `code:<relative path>` under the tracked code root. An absolute path is refused, upward traversal is refused, and a symlinked target is refused wherever it points - the same target rule commitments/schema.json states, for the same reason.
args.integrity: package-relative command that verifies package integrity before use
args.setup: package-relative command that creates disposable candidate state
args.verify: package-relative command that grades it and prints the result
args.controls: package-relative command that proves the oracle is red-capable

fixture_oracle.absent_package_is_could_not_observe: The package may live in a home's gitignored data/, so a tracked contract can name one this checkout does not have. That is COULD_NOT_OBSERVE - the predicate could not run - and never a pass and never a failure.

generation_manifest.where: MANIFEST.json under the declared `root`, which is the same file `manifest_digest` already pins. No second location and no new declaration: the manifest is already the package's identity, so making it the carrier costs a contract nothing.
generation_manifest.predicates_unchanged_from: OPTIONAL object mapping a BASE manifest digest to the array of claim ids this generation declares materially unchanged from it. A record graded under that base digest whose every failed claim id appears in the array keeps its adverse retry disposition in this generation.
generation_manifest.why_the_absence_is_the_default: A generation that declares nothing about a base generation's claims has replaced them, so retry is permitted. Requiring an explicit `predicates_changed` list instead would make forgetting to write one silently freeze a binding out forever, which is the failure this register is least able to notice. Forgetting the carry-forward list has the opposite failure - one re-run of a binding that would have failed again - and that one is bounded, visible and cheap.
generation_manifest.reading_it_is_could_not_observe_when_the: Same rule as the predicate itself. An absent or unreadable manifest leaves the disposition `unknown`, which withholds the invocation; it is never read as an absent declaration, because those are different facts.

declared_deterministic.description: The predicate is a named executable check inside this repository that needs no candidate at all.

args.check: path to the executable, resolved only under the tracked code root
args.expect: the exact stdout token that means pass

freshness_dependency_kinds._rule: A closed set, and every record declares its dependencies explicitly. A dependency kind the interpreter cannot probe is permitted, and is then ALWAYS MARKED as uncovered and never read as unchanged - but a record that declares an uncovered dependency must also declare a time_bound, or it is INADMISSIBLE.
freshness_dependency_kinds._why_the_time_bound_rule_exists: Two failures are available here and only one is survivable. Forcing every unprobeable dependency to COULD_NOT_OBSERVE makes every record permanently unusable, which defeats the ruling it implements. Letting one pass silently means a harness upgrade can change semantics under a QUALIFIED record and nothing notices. The rule takes the third option the ruling itself names: what cannot be probed is BOUNDED IN TIME instead, so the record expires on its own rather than either shouting forever or going quietly wrong.

file_digest.description: The sha256 of a named file. Probeable. This is how fixture bytes, oracle bytes and contract bytes are pinned.

args.path: resolved only under the tracked code root or under FM_HOME, by the same `code:`/`home:` prefix rule predicate_kinds states
args.digest: the sha256 observed at qualification time

file_digest.absent_file: COULD_NOT_OBSERVE on this dependency. An absent file is not an unchanged one.

contract_version.description: The contract's own declared version. Probeable from the contract file.

args.version: the contract_version observed at qualification time

time_bound.description: A justified expiry. Probeable against today's date.

args.until: ISO date (YYYY-MM-DD) after which this observation no longer applies
args.justification: one sentence: why this bound, rather than a round number

harness_semantics.description: The harness's behavior relevant to this run, recorded as a version string. UNCOVERED: nothing here probes a harness version, because doing so is a harness-dependent check that would need a live per-harness guard to be worth anything, and a check that only confirms the assumption written into its own stub is worse than an honest gap.

args.version: the version observed at qualification time

binding_semantics.description: The provider-side semantics of the exact model. UNCOVERED: providers publish no snapshot identifier this fleet can read, which every qualification run so far recorded as a limitation rather than papering over.

args.observed: whatever identity the provider did expose, or COULD_NOT_OBSERVE

native_effort_mapping.description: That the named native effort still maps to the reasoning depth it did. UNCOVERED for the same reason as harness_semantics.

args.observed: how it was established, or COULD_NOT_OBSERVE

route_integration.requires_capabilities: A route floor in config/crew-dispatch.json may declare `requires_capabilities`: an array of contract ids every candidate must hold a QUALIFIED record for. Absent means this register changes nothing for that route, which is how a home that never opted in stays exactly as capable as it was. Present means the gate fails CLOSED: an unreadable register, an absent record and an unobservable dependency all withhold the candidate, because a declared requirement whose evidence cannot be read has not been met.
route_integration.why_this_gate_does_not_fail_open: The quota gate deliberately fails toward dispatch because an unobserved quota can only ever REMOVE a candidate the policy already admitted. This one is the opposite shape: it is the requirement itself, so failing to observe it would admit a candidate on no evidence, which is the exact substitution the ruling forbids.

zero_route_classification._description: When a route has no eligible candidate, the answer is not one fact. bin/fm-route-lib.sh classifies it deterministically from the per-candidate blocker sets, and only one classification escalates.
zero_route_classification.QUALIFICATION_REQUIRED: At least one candidate is blocked SOLELY by missing or stale qualification WHOSE RETRY IS PERMITTED. Engineering state: one bounded qualification workflow is activated for the cheapest promising candidate. Escalation NONE.
zero_route_classification.QUALIFICATION_COULD_NOT_OBSERVE: No candidate is fixable by qualifying it, but at least one is blocked solely because its qualification, or its retry disposition, could not be observed. Nonterminal: the repair is to the register. Escalation NONE, and no new negative is recorded against any binding.
zero_route_classification.AWAITING_AVAILABILITY: Every remaining candidate is blocked only by an availability hold or spent capacity. A wait, owned by the existing availability and capacity-deferral paths. Escalation NONE.
zero_route_classification.NO_MODEL_CAN_SATISFY_ROUTE: Every candidate is excluded by something qualifying it cannot fix: a floor axis it does not meet, a model-registry refusal, a FAILED qualification whose dependencies have not changed, or a retry the register refuses because the material predicate the binding failed has not changed. Escalation CAPTAIN_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED.
zero_route_classification.the_one_thing_this_must_never_do: Missing qualification alone must never produce CAPTAIN_EXCEPTION_REQUIRED. That is the recurrence this whole register exists to close, and tests/fm-route-qualification.test.sh pins it with a mutation control.
zero_route_classification.the_second_thing_this_must_never_do: A candidate whose retry disposition is not `permitted` must never appear as promising. It is excluded as `qualification_retry_not_permitted`, which joins the escalating bucket exactly as a preserved FAILED record does, or as `qualification_retry_cno`, which joins the unobservable one. Collapsing the second into the first would report a gap in the register as a settled refusal of the binding, and collapsing either into `qualification_missing` is the defect that made a version bump reopen a known failure.

route_integration.cheapest_promising_ordering: Promising candidates are ordered by recorded price ascending, then by pool position. A candidate whose price cannot be observed sorts LAST rather than first: unmeasured cost must never read as cheap, which is the same rule the model registry already applies to an unclassified provider.

bounded_workflow.identity: A deterministic tuple identity is derived from the whole record key - contract, model, harness and native effort - by an unambiguous encoding. At most one incarnation for that tuple may be open; after a prior incarnation is Done, requalification uses the next numeric incarnation so stale or materially changed evidence can activate again without colliding with retained backlog history.
bounded_workflow.the_workflow_is_a_backlog_task: A bounded qualification workflow IS a work item, so it is registered as one through the existing backlog owner. That is what makes `tasks-axi block --by` meet its documented precondition that the blocker must already exist, rather than working around it.
bounded_workflow.one_durable_fact: The workflow's backlog record is the ONLY fact about whether it is live. The blocked work's dependency on it is not a second copy: bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh recomputes unresolved_blocker_ids on every read and resolves a blocker exactly when its structured record is Done. The relationship is therefore DERIVED on read by an owner that already exists, exactly as qualification state is computed on read and expired availability holds are dropped on read rather than swept.
bounded_workflow.why_there_is_no_compensation_logic: DELIBERATE, and this is the note a future reader should find instead of an absence. An earlier design stored the workflow's liveness in its own record AND mirrored it into a backlog edge. Five review rounds each found a different way for those two facts to disagree: a predecessor blocker left behind on advancement, a half-written block reported as active, an unblock that could not be retried after a terminal write failed. Intermediate states, transfer logic, compensation and retry reconciliation are all machinery that exists BECAUSE something is mirrored. Nothing is mirrored now, so those findings are closed BY CONSTRUCTION rather than patched, and there is nothing left for a reconciliation path to reconcile. Do not add one back without first re-introducing a second liveness fact, which is the thing to avoid.
bounded_workflow.the_defect_this_also_fixed: tasks-axi block refuses a blocker that is not itself a task, and bin/fm-fleet-snapshot.sh leaves a blocker with no record open forever. The mirrored edge was therefore never written, and could never have resolved if it had been - the design did not function at all. Five rounds of review missed it because the test fixture's fake tasks-axi exited 0 unconditionally; tests/lib.sh's fm_fake_tasks_axi now reproduces the real refusals and a control pins it against the real binary.
bounded_workflow.bound: bin/fm-attempt.sh over the ACTIVATION's own identity. The blocked work identity's attempt count, retry budget and custody bases are never read, spent or reset by a qualification workflow.
bounded_workflow.no_second_scheduler: The worker is launched through bin/fm-spawn.sh, the one chokepoint, so route, admission, capacity, cost, entitlement and concurrency are all re-evaluated there and nowhere else.
bounded_workflow.bootstrap: The CANDIDATE is the worker. It is dispatched on a bootstrap route it ALREADY qualifies for, whose floor meets the target floor's axes, and it runs the real work - so the register holds evidence about the candidate because the candidate is what executed. The already-qualified binding supplies the route the dispatch runs on; it is not the worker and never writes a record about a run it did not do. There is deliberately no exemption for the qualifying run: exempting it would weaken the standard it exists to establish, and a candidate with no bootstrap route is a stop-and-report rather than a licence to self-certify.
bounded_workflow.on_pass: The workflow item is closed. THAT is what returns the blocked work to normal eligibility, because the blocker resolves when its record is Done. Its identity, custody and budget are untouched, and no unblock call exists to fail after the fact.
bounded_workflow.on_failure: The FAILED record is retained as exclusion evidence. Every dependent identity is derived from the fleet snapshot's backlog edges, never copied into another store. The next promising candidate is activated FIRST for every dependent so the successor already holds every dependency, and only then is this item closed. Reversed, a successor that failed to register would leave work eligible with nothing qualified.
bounded_workflow.on_could_not_observe: Nonterminal. One attempt is spent and no record of incapability is written. When the bound is exhausted, the item stays open and receives a parked hold through the backlog owner naming the Firstmate decision to raise the bound or abandon the qualification; it is never marked Done without an observed terminal outcome.
